USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

Sexual adverse effect

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 29-year-old man has improved mood and energy after 6 weeks of sertraline but reports new delayed ejaculation. The symptom began after treatment; libido and sexual function had been normal before it. He takes no other medications. Which interpretation is most appropriate?

  1. Proof that the depression has worsened
  2. A diagnostic feature of serotonin syndrome
  3. Evidence of irreversible testicular failure
  4. An expected consequence of dopamine D2 blockade
  5. A recognized SSRI-associated sexual adverse effect
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

A recognized SSRI-associated sexual adverse effect

Temporal association and the known adverse-effect pattern support discussing medication-related dysfunction rather than dismissing it.

Understanding the options

A recognized SSRI-associated sexual adverse effect
Temporal association and the known adverse-effect pattern support discussing medication-related dysfunction rather than dismissing it.
Proof that the depression has worsened
His mood and energy have improved, and the new timing suggests a medication contribution.
A diagnostic feature of serotonin syndrome
Isolated delayed ejaculation does not establish systemic serotonin toxicity.
Evidence of irreversible testicular failure
The history does not establish gonadal failure or irreversibility.
An expected consequence of dopamine D2 blockade
Sertraline is not a D2-blocking antipsychotic.
